entities.summary: Cephisodotus the Elder (c. 500 BCE) was a renowned ancient Greek musician and composer of the Classical era, active in Athens, Greece. He was a key figure in the development of ancient Greek music and dance, and his works were performed during the Olympic Games in Olympia, Greece. Cephisodotus's significance extends to his contributions to the preservation of ancient Greek culture and his influence on later Greek musical traditions. He was also known for his work as a painter and sculptor, and his artistic skills were highly regarded by his contemporaries. Cephisodotus's legacy can be seen in the many surviving fragments of his music and the impact he had on the development of Western classical music. In particular, his contributions to the development of the aulos, a ancient Greek double reed instrument, had a lasting impact on the evolution of Western classical music. The aulos, which was popularized by Cephisodotus, remained a staple instrument in Greek music for centuries, influencing the development of later musical instruments and styles.
